collections.name: The Works of Frits Albers
collections.tagline: Catholic author, scholar, theologian, witness to the Faith. Faith, history, ideas that endure.
intro: This collection of the works of Frits Albers contains nine stand-alone books and four volumes of selected works. The four volumes of selected works contain, between them, twelve books that were each first published as stand-alone books. Consequently, the total number of books contained in the list below is actually twenty-one.

It can be seen from his biography that the life of Frits Albers (1921 – 2000), a sincere Dutch-born Catholic, emigrating to Australia after the Second World War, placed him, quasi-providentially, one might say, in an almost perfect position to judge the changes and turmoil that had come upon his Church in the first early years after the Second Vatican Council.

As a young man in the 1940s, he was educated by Jesuits who were, in a real way, the instigators of the ‘new Catholicism’ of Teilhard de Chardin SJ and disseminated it widely (think of the notorious “Dutch Catechism”). Right from the start, the perceived need for “updating” the Church’s relation with the World was being used (abused) to make the Church conform to the World’s fashions of thought and practice (call them secularist or modernist as you please).

The clear mind of the now mature Frits got on to what was happening immediately, and in the following 30 years to the date of his death he wrote a collection of works aimed at showing up the work of deceit of the multitude of propagators of the new “Spirit” claimed to be found in the Council.  Just how powerful his critiques are, one will find on reading them. One cannot fail to notice how telling his insights were at the time and, most importantly, how even more relevant they are to our own times.

Frits Albers focused on the areas of Catholic teaching and pastoral practice that mainly came under attack, ranging from the most exalted levels of the Eucharist and the Mother of God to more general dilution of principal doctrines and traditional disciplines. If anything, the attacks have intensified since his time, which is a reason it is more urgent to have his books today. Indeed, he focused particularly on the push for a false ecumenism to be found in the imprudent association of the Catholic hierarchy with the organisation called the World Council of Churches (WCC).

Any one of his books may be read with profit and not surprisingly with a feeling of relief and joy. We recommend, however, starting with the three connected books entitled “The Beyerhaus Effect”, “The World Council of Churches” and “On Judging, Conscience and Predestination”, since they provide a good background.

Frits Albers’ books are written in the clear light of a strong and vibrant Catholic Faith and are thoroughly grounded in the philosophy of St. Thomas Aquinas, especially in practical moral principles. From a philosophical perspective, they closely align with Don Boland’s books on the philosophy of St. Thomas Aquinas.

collections.name: The Writings of Dr. Donald G. Boland
collections.tagline: Scholar, historian, author, defender of the Faith. Twelve books on the philosophy of St. Thomas Aquinas.
intro: The twelve books shown below are based on the work of St. Thomas Aquinas. Though much is contained in his theological writings, the aim is philosophical which, as Aquinas famously says, commenting on Aristotle in In de caelo, is not to know what many, including Aristotle himself, may have thought, but "the truth of thing" (veritas rei).

Hence, the object is to cover the whole scope of philosophy and science so as to bring out the full range of natural reason that can be found in Aquinas’s writings, if mainly in his commentaries on Aristotle. This everyone will readily appreciate is an aim, even at the level of human reason, that is hardly reachable without divine assistance.

Aquinas, as a person of Faith, evidently had such assistance, so has been accorded by the highest teaching authority on earth–the Magisterium of the Catholic Church, founded by Jesus Christ, the Son of God–the majestic title of Common Doctor (Universal Teacher), not just on matters of Faith but also of Reason, though the latter is principally concerned with natural wisdom (Metaphysics) and practical reason (Morals). This evidently does not extend to where St. Thomas is speaking tentatively and merely expressing an opinion (as does Aristotle), especially in many cases of natural philosophy or science.

The author does not make any claim to perfection or completeness in presenting, according to his limited capacity, the genial grasp of Aquinas (and Aristotle) of “the truth of thing”. His intent is to bring the gist of the writings of Aquinas on philosophy to the notice of all who are either sadly unaware of his works, or, for one reason or another, know of his works in a widely misrepresented or misinterpreted way, even in current Catholic educational institutions.
“I truly believe as time passes this unique series will be more and more sought after by those who want a really good education in the philosophy of St Thomas Aquinas and much more besides.”
– Frank Calneggia, editor of many of these works below and author of
A Series on Various Modern-Day Thinkers and Events

Donald G Boland, Ll. B. (Sydney), Ph. D. (Angelicum), is a founding member of the Centre for Catholic Studies Inc. in Sydney, Australia, and served as its president. He practiced for a number of years as a lawyer having a degree in law from the University of Sydney. Over much the same time, having obtained a doctorate in philosophy from the University of St. Thomas in Rome, he has taught philosophy and law in both Catholic and secular educational institutions, such as the University of Technology, Sydney, the University of Newcastle, the Aquinas Academy, the Centre for Thomistic Studies Inc., now operating under the name of the Centre for Catholic Studies Inc., and various Catholic seminaries, such as those of the Marists and the Vincentians.
